OrangeSalon/651-PowersOfHorror/Powers-of.content:
Chapter 1
Neither Subject Nor Object
We’re dealing here with the subject object distinction and how it relates to the abject.
What is the subject object distinction?  Subject and object are both grammatical as well as philosophical terms, and it can be helpful to understand the latter through the former.  Subjects are beings which do, which can think and act.  Objects are, of course, those things which are acted upon, or referred to.  It can be helpful to loosely think of it as the distinction between first and third person.  Importantly, what is a subject in one context might be an object in another.  You have your own thoughts and interiority, but I can only ever grasp you through what I see in front of me.  The context in which we are using subject/object here is in relation to consciousness.  The subject is the conscious being, while the object is the object of consciousness.  The object of consciousness is what consciousness is about.  Any thought or sensation that we may have is always about something.  In the tradition of analytic philosophy, this property of consciousness as being about something is referred to as intentionality, and it is seen as a fundamental feature of consciousness.
Kristeva is writing in the psychoanalytic tradition.  One of the primary features of psychoanalysis is its emphasis on a developmental view on consciousness and its conception of the unconscious.  Accordingly, consciousness and intentionality are not taken for granted, but are considered as emerging out of complex social and developmental processes as essentially useful fictions or half-truths that serve to represent or signify more fundamental animal or ontological drives.  Psychoanalysis does not take the self-presentation of consciousness at face value, and so it is possible to speak of the “motion” or “movement” of objects in consciousness.
The abject takes this destabilization of the subject/object distinction further by positing the existence of something ‘like’ an object but which is not an object, which is defined in fact by not being an object, the (a)bject.  The question is why the abject is not an object.  Kristeva describes this as ‘jettisoning’ or ‘radical exclusion,’ and attributes this exclusion to the superego.  We’ll see later on that the superego is actually the primary source of abjection.
Terminology
affect - a perturbation in self understood as a sensation or feeling
ego - part of the Freudian ternary system, the ego is one’s self-image
superego - the superego is the voice of commandment, law, it is both stupid and all-knowing
unconscious - in psychoanalysis, the unconscious refers to the complex of desires, drives, and sensations that are unknown to the analysand and to general waking conscious, but which structure consciousness
The Improper / Unclean
This is probably the most difficult section of the chapter because Kristeva is giving a psychoanalytic, developmental account of abjection here without explicitly stating that that is what she is doing.
The section on food-loathing and the interaction with the milk-skin is written from the perspective of a child being fed by their parents.  The child establishes herself as individual by the rejection of the parent’s will, through abjecting herself.  By vomiting out the food or disgusting substance, the child separates herself from the will and desires of the parent.  The child herself becomes disgusting in order to establish herself as herself, outside of the parents desires or symbolic system.
Terminology
Signified / Signifier - Coming from semiotics, heavily used by Lacan, the signifier / signified distinction is the distinction between a representation and what it represents.  Importantly, for many semioticians there is no ultimate signified.  Rather, signs always refer to other signs, and it is in this circularity that meaning is established.  Words, pictures, sounds, gestures, anything can be a signifier.  For Lacan, the phallus is the stand in for the master signfiier
The Abjection of Self
Context
Emptiness of Self - Psychoanalysis holds that there is no fundamental self, with the closest thing being the wound or lack of self which we all experience as a result of being separated from the Mother, aka the state in which all of ours needs are met immediately and we want for nothing
Mysticism - The religious practice of direct communion with the divine through rituals, self-denial, starvation, and solitude
Beyond the Unconscious
Kristeva is here talking about some of the implications of her conception of abjection for psychoanalytic theorization and practice.  She posits that, just as neurosis and psychosis stem from disorders in desire, disorders in abjection create their own form of pathology.  At root is the contrast she draws between object and abject.  Since abjection blurs the subject-object distinction (since the abject do not rise to the level of objects,) the standard methods of understanding pathology fall away, since at root they are based on disorders in desire, which is always desire for an object (the objet petit a).  Because of this, disorders in abjection short-circuit the typical repressive frameworks, leading to statements of desires that would typically be unconscious.
This also furthers our understanding of abjection, emphasizing its method of operation - exclusion, in contrast with negation.
Terminology
Dialectic - From Hegel, a dialectic is a constitutive relation of negation which is inseparable from the identity of a thing.  In this text, the unconscious is a dialectic of negation, that is, it is the result of the inseparability and contradiction that results from the relation of negation and positivity
Judgment - Judgment should be understood as the application of our mental faculties to the world, it is deciding that something is such and such, that it falls under such and such concept or idea
An Exile Who Asks, “Where?”
Continuing our emphasis on abjection as exclusion, with particular focus on the spatial character of exclusion.
Time: Forgetfulness and Thunder / Jouissance and Affect
Terminology
Jouissance - In Lacanian thought, jouissance is a forbidden / painful pleasure.  Honestly not too sure on this one, it’s pretty important for Lacan though.
At The Limit of Primal Repression
Terminology
Primal Repression - More Freudian jargon.  Basically, the state of entering into consciousness, the repression of primal drives
a posteriori / a priori - posteriori knowledge is knowledge after the fact, such as scientific knowledge, while a priori knowledge is knowledge prior to the fact, such as mathematical knowledge
Premises of the Sign, Linings of the Sublime
Terminology
Sublime - The sublime is the experience of the infinite, that which is in excess of our representational powers which overwhelms us
Before the Beginning: Separation
Terminology
mimesis - The process of coming to resemble or mimic a thing
”The Chora”, Receptacle of Narcissism
Terminology
aporia - A state of speechlessness resulting from the failure of thought or conceptual thinking

OrangeSalon/Orange-Salon-Site.title: Orange Salon Site
OrangeSalon/Orange-Salon-Site.content:
I’m currently using Quartz as a static site generator to upload the contents of my obsidian vault as html.  The problem is that I frequently will reference other notes in my Powers of Horror notes, and I need a way to include only those notes that are referenced without using anything else.
Using Quartz
To build quartz, run
npx quartz create

To run quartz, run
npx quartz build --serve

Parsing
To that end I’ve been using obsidianmd-parser which is a python parser for obsidian files.  On Ubuntu, I’ve created a folder called webdev in my home directory.  In that folder, I have a pipenv setup pipenv run python (x.py) with the obsidian-md parser library installed.  Right now I’m building a program that will recursively go through and create symlinks for each link in the notes.
